NOVELTY STATEMENT
USER CONSTRAINT: Standard practice delivers a monitoring/indication scheme using temperature and flow measurements to detect fouling.
CALCULATED: My mechanism departs by using the time derivative of the heat transfer coefficient calculated from existing measurements, rather than absolute values or simple delta-T thresholds.
USER CONSTRAINT: This works because fouling accumulation follows an asymptotic growth curve, where the rate of degradation accelerates significantly before reaching critical levels.

PHYSICS CHECK
USER CONSTRAINT: Governing physical relation: Q = U·A·ΔT_lm (heat transfer rate = overall heat transfer coefficient × area × log mean temperature difference)
CALCULATED: For a condenser with fouling, U decreases as fouling resistance R_f increases: 1/U = 1/U_clean + R_f
CALCULATED: The time derivative dU/dt will show an accelerating negative slope as fouling accumulates, typically 3-4 weeks before reaching critical derating levels.
CALCULATED: Typical U degradation rate in MW condensers is 0.5-2% per week at normal conditions, accelerating to 5-10%/week in the final 3 weeks before derating.

USER CONSTRAINT: Materials (none required beyond existing infrastructure)

USER CONSTRAINT: Procedure:
1. Calculate hourly heat transfer coefficient U from existing measurements: U = Q/(A·ΔT_lm)
2. Calculate 24-hour rolling average of U to filter noise
3. Calculate weekly rate of change of U: dU/dt (%/week)
4. Trigger alert when dU/dt exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive days
